results.description:
FUNAAB, Chinese Investors Move to Finalise MoU on 7-Hectare Commercial Hatchery Project

By Olasunkanmi Olajide
 
The Federal University of Agriculture, Abeokuta (FUNAAB), Nigeria, is poised to seal a strategic industry-academia partnership with Chinese investors for the establishment of a modern commercial hatchery farm on seven hectares of land within the campus.

The proposed project, promoted by Olagen Agritech Nigeria FZE, would integrate breeder chicken production and egg hatching, with the potential to strengthen Nigeria’s poultry value chain, enhance food security, facilitate technology transfer and create employment opportunities for young people.

The initiative follows a working visit to FUNAAB on September 22, 2026, during which discussions focused on land cooperation, project implementation and the development of a mutually beneficial partnership between the University and the prospective investors.

At a follow-up meeting held today, October 20, 2026, the Vice-Chancellor, Prof. Babatunde Kehinde, expressed the University’s readiness to facilitate the project within the framework of a mutually agreed contractual arrangement. He reaffirmed FUNAAB’s capacity to enter into lawful partnerships with private-sector organisations to advance agricultural development, research and innovation.

The proposed Memorandum of Understanding (MoU), expected to be signed soon, would establish the framework for the development and operation of the commercial hatchery farm, subject to the final terms agreed upon by both parties.

Beyond commercial poultry production, the proposed partnership is expected to promote international academic engagement, while exposing participants to modern hatchery technologies, improved poultry production systems and international agricultural best practices.  

The initiative would reinforce FUNAAB’s commitment to industry-academia collaboration, technology-driven agribusiness and practical agricultural education. It would also present opportunities for knowledge exchange, capacity development and the application of innovative solutions to challenges facing Nigeria’s poultry industry.

Upon implementation, the project is expected to contribute to national food security, youth employment, agricultural innovation and sustainable economic growth, while strengthening agricultural cooperation between Nigeria and China.

results.title: Modern Nigerian rail projects since 2016 are independent of Britain.
results.description:
Modern Nigerian rail projects since 2016 are independent of Britain. Abuja-Kaduna (2016) and Lagos-Ibadan (2021) standard-gauge lines were built by China's CCECC with Chinese loans. Warri-Itakpe standard gauge finished 2020. Kano-Maradi (to Niger) uses Portuguese contractors, near completion. Kaduna-Kano ongoing with fresh Chinese funding. Old Cape-gauge colonial tracks are separate and largely obsolete.

Next decade: complete Lagos-Kano corridor, 4000 km high-speed network (350 km/h), expand to 10,000+ km, electrify and switch to LNG power. All Nigerian-led with China, private and other partners.

results.title: SLIPPERY IVE NOT GONE ANYWHERE BLAIR STRIKES AGAIN......
results.description:
SLIPPERY IVE NOT GONE ANYWHERE BLAIR STRIKES AGAIN......
The Tony Blair institute  has spent years advising Nigeria's president on trade , power and agriculture and a British Lithium firm says its mining leases were revoked and handed to Chinese interests whilst Blairs people were in the romm.
Jupiter Lithium claims it found deposits big enough to supply Britain for decades, protected under a UK/Nigeria treaty then lost everything .
Blairs office says mining was never discussed.
Nigeria calls it a smear .
Either way a declared UK national security priority just slipped through Britain's fingers and the man who was supposed to be helping is the one with questions to answer ....

results.title: No exhaustive public list exists of every Tinubu-era foreign investment that has produced confirmed Nigerian jobs.
results.description:
No exhaustive public list exists of every Tinubu-era foreign investment that has produced confirmed Nigerian jobs. Actual FDI inflows remain far below announced pledges.

Examples include the Chinese $250m lithium plant in Nasarawa (Diamond New Energy), which reports over 1,000 direct and 2,000 indirect jobs, and the $200m Zamfara plant (Chinese partners) targeting 2,000 local jobs. The $7bn Ogun DP World seaport deal is still an MoU projecting 50,000 jobs.
